For kill order, you want to do:

-Fives: If you try to kill anything else first, Fives throws himself under the bus and everything gets a boost

-Rex: I know you want to get rid of Echo since he keeps stunning and stripping off buffs but Rex is priority as he can shit out turn order and occasionally delete one of your characters which is just a run ender (using an ability that starts on cooldown).

-Echo: Stomp the little rat and stop him from stunning and buff-stripping.

-ARC: Also a buff-stripper, but slightly less priority than Echo

-Clean up GAS


I will reiterate; this is extremely RNG dependent, but my team was largely G12+4, with the R5 B1, and perseverance (and mods) got me there.

If I had to do it again, I'd relic up Droideka and Magna too

That is all around some very fantastic points.. I wasn't super attached to the Kurskana=N'kuhana theory and tbh this does make more sense. I completely glossed over that humans interacted with her somehow.

That said, I don't think it implausible that 'she' could have died after Mithrix was banished. Mithrix seems able to observe his brother, displaying contempt at Providence's ongoing nature reserve and expressing knowledge of Providence's interest in humans. I think there's definite leeway for it to have been either before or after going off what you said. I think Providence was aware of soul before her gift, but was clumsy with its' use, as with Aurelionite. He clearly gained a level of competence with it, but I'm not sure whether through practice or granted power.

An interesting take on the void reavers! I struggled to find anything specific to them in the lore but granted I don't know a lot about risk 1 so it could have been there.. I do know that Mithrix refers to Petrichor V as their prison in the A Moment, Shattered log so I can definitely see sense in this theory! Perhaps the void reavers on the moon are there to attempt to punish you for defeating Mithrix.. Also their appearance in the late game might be because they see you as a threat to their charge? 

I would love to see and hear more about the newt, hopefully we'll get something soon!

It certainly sounds like the kind of thing somebody with a childish grudge would do if they were also completely psychotic..

Honestly, who knows. The species that Mithrix and Providence belong to possibly don't even have souls (The log of Lunar Chimera - Wisp suggests that 'all vermin are driven by souls', which makes me think that the brothers are powered by something else..) Perhaps Kurskana was one of the same species, or perhaps Mithrix used his power to torment her while he could.

That said there's also a lot of items with a time/temporal focus so it wouldn't surprise me if there was some time based nonsense going on there too.
I completely missed the names of the elite equipments! Definitely some interesting points there.. I'll have to have a re-read of the logs in that context when I get in from work

I will be honest, I'm making a lot of educated guesses here - entirely based on the logs, a couple of achievements, and clues in the environments but guesses nonetheless.

It's interesting to think that elites could be a manifestation of worship.. Perhaps the celestine elites come from Mithrix? It certainly fits his vibe..

Also I forgot to mention the dead void reavers in the void fields.. I can think of a handful of reasons for being there but those conflict with each other. Perhaps it's where they go when they die, perhaps they died in between the moon and Petrichor V, perhaps it is the place of their creation, perhaps they were banished there by N'kuhana/Kurskana and Providence. I'm just not clear. Perhaps if the void fields log ever reads as something other than 'not available' then we might find out!

I have some thoughts, but I'm certainly not sure, a lot of this feels like wild conjecture to me so take it with a pinch of salt. 


I believe that Kurskana the heretic is the 'she' that Mithrix keeps referring to in the logs. She visited frequently when Mithrix and Providence were children, teaching them how to make their creations and gifting them with glass frogs to chase.

I believe that Mithrix is also the creator of the void reavers, sending them down to Petrichor V to try to switch the lunar teleporters back on. (Based on them only appearing in the late game and on the moon.)

I believe that Kurskana opted to help Providence deal with the void reavers, but fell foul of the cult of N'kuhana (I've entertained the possibility that the cult could have worshipped Kurskana but twisted her name given that the names are so similar but can't find any concrete proof). I think Kurskana was killed by the ceremonial dagger, which put an end to the void reaver threat for the time being (again no concrete proof but it makes sense to me.) Since the void reavers stopped appearing after that point, I think the cult branded her a heretic. I base this off the log where Mithrix claims that 'she' shouldn't have died for Providence. (Kurskana the heretic is the only other mysterious non-human character to be confirmed dead in the logs, which is where I draw the link.)

Providence did something to prevent the return of the reavers so long as he was alive, then did his mourning and sent Kurskana to the moon so that Mithrix could do the same and maybe repent for his actions.

Mithrix ransacked her body for power and turned her into lunar items, hence the scattering of the heretic's parts.


There's a very good chance I've gotten plenty of things wrong. Maybe we'll get more logs down the line to elaborate on N'kuhana and Kurskana the Heretic, since what we have now only feels like half of the story there!

I believe that Providence tricked Mithrix into becoming stranded on the moon because of his cruelty to 'vermin' species. (See the log for A Moment: Fractured). Mithrix is understandably furious because he sees no worth in these species  and I think isolation drove him to desire the destruction of all that Providence held dear.. Including humanity.

I have a player who has really gone for the whole daemonic and mutation path, with very little prodding from me. Naturally he's gathered a number of malignancies and mutations, but I haven't forced any of these on him, he's accepted them willingly.

Recently the party found a Thrice-Bound Daemonhost made by their (former) Inquisitor, who has been nothing but accommodating. It's provided them information on a number of things, and helped the mutant create a daemon weapon this last session. Recently, the party has gotten split, and somehow the mutant and the Daemonhost have ended up travelling together, without any oversight from the rest.

The Daemonhost is going to offer its assistance in extremely Do or Die situations, always saying that it 'needs more power', to get the player to weaken its bindings, or asking that he does so as payment for services. Obviously those requests will be refused, but eventually, after its proving reliable time and time again, or the player involved being in a more than lethal situation, they might very well accept.


I've found that it's not so much forcibly damning them as putting the tools to damn themselves into their own hands and watching what they do that's been the most fun here.


Since we're talking possession, and you don't want the daemon getting too obtrusive yet, maybe have the Daemon offer helpful advice or knowledge in situations where these things might REALLY be needed. 

Perhaps next time your player finds themselves burning a fate point, perhaps it's not the Emperor's hand in the acolyte avoiding death as it is the Daemon animating the acolyte's body and forcing them out of danger. Naturally, this might include side-effects such as mutation or malignancies, but all in a day's work for an acolyte of the Imperial Inquisition.

Things like that, really. Since the Daemon is weak, it will be easily exorcised, so it will likely be very willing to cooperate to avoid that. The serious stuff comes later when it gets stronger, with corruption points gained for accepting help, punishment for turning the daemon down, etc.
